text:
incident-bot: 🚨 *Perf Canary Regression Alert* (SEV-3)
- Signal: p95_latency_ms regression
- Slice: model=llama-3-70b-instruct region=us-east gpu_sku=A100-80GB scheduler_mode=prod-default
- Current: +22% vs baseline (7d median)
- Window: last 10m (min_samples met)
- Dash: https://grafana.redwood.inference/d/perf-canary/perf-canary?var-model=llama-3-70b-instruct&var-region=us-east&var-gpu=A100-80GB
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.inference/display/SRE/Runbook%3A+Perf+Canary+Regression+Triage
- Recent deploys: runtime_version=1.18.0-rc3 (git_sha=9f2c1d7)

Sean Gallagher: ack. pulling dash now. anyone else seeing customer impact or just canary?

Rafael Mendes: :eyes: checking prod latency SLO board. canary only atm, customer p95 looks flat-ish but canary is clean signal.

Tomáš Novák: starting triage checklist. first: verify sample size + no maintenance window.

Allison Grant: fyi dedup key is model+region+gpu+runtime_build, so this is the only page for the slice.

deploy-bot: *Deploy event* runtime us-east
- Service: serving-runtime
- Version: 1.18.0-rc3
- Time: 1736821668
- Change: "scheduler: enable heuristic_x" (release-candidate)

Mateo Alvarez: online. this lines up w/ rc3 rollout in us-east. can we confirm regression is isolated to A100 slice?

Marcus Reed: from canary dashboard: A100-80GB slice regressed, H100 slice looks steady (maybe not enough samples yet). tokens/sec panel also down ~8%.

Sofia Ivanova: heuristic_x was supposed to be guarded behind feature flag; did it end up on by default for canary traffic too?

Omar El-Sayed: canary requests are tagged `source=perf-canary` + `request_class=canary-safe` but they still use scheduler_mode=prod-default unless pinned. for this slice it’s prod-default.

Tomáš Novák: runbook step 2: check noise/warmup. this is 10m+ sustained and starts right after deploy annotation. looks real.

Sean Gallagher: agree. propose mitigation: roll back runtime to rc2 in us-east, keep canary running to confirm.

Rafael Mendes: +1. if we roll back quickly we avoid even potential customer drift. SEV-3 is ok.

Mateo Alvarez: do it. also want a quick kernel-selection dump if possible before rollback (canary-gated export) so we have a clue.

Hiro Tanaka: i can grab kernel selection logs from a canary pod if Omar can point me at the request ids.

Omar El-Sayed: pulling a trace sample now. latest canary span ids from the panel:
- trace: 7b1c9f0a2c4d
- trace: 91aa0d3ef112
we should see `selected_kernel_id` + `fallback_reason` in attributes.

Logan Wright: from telemetry side: metrics look consistent (no missing labels). windowing is correct on this panel (we fixed mismatch earlier). so not a pipeline artifact.

Nadia Rahman: confirming aggregation: p95 over 5m buckets, alert compares last 10m vs 7d median at same time-of-day band. so baseline should be stable.

deploy-bot: Rolling back serving-runtime in us-east...
- from: 1.18.0-rc3 (9f2c1d7)
- to: 1.18.0-rc2 (5c0a8b1)
- reason: perf-canary regression

Hiro Tanaka: got kernel selection for one of those traces. looks like it switched to kernel_id=attn_fused_v14 w/ reason="heuristic_x". previously was v12 for this prompt shape.

Sofia Ivanova: that’s suspicious. heuristic_x likely changing prefill/decode packing. canary prompt shape is the 4k prefill / 256 decode variant right?

Marcus Reed: yep for llama-3-70b-instruct in us-east: prefill=4096, decode=256. streaming=on. (from matrix config)

Sean Gallagher: watching dash. p95 is already trending down as rollback drains.

Tomáš Novák: should we add suppression during rollback to avoid duplicate pages? (maintenance window for us-east runtime)

Sean Gallagher: yes, add a 30m maintenance suppression for the perf-canary service in us-east while deploy completes.

Allison Grant: done. added temporary maintenance window in slo-toolkit; expires in 30m.

Rafael Mendes: customer board still stable. no open SUPs linked.

Mateo Alvarez: good. action items: revert heuristic_x default OR pin canary scheduler settings to avoid mixing with new heuristics during early rollout.

Sofia Ivanova: +1 on pinning for canary. also we need a safe rollout plan so canary sees the new scheduler mode explicitly as a separate slice.

Omar El-Sayed: canary has support for `scheduler_mode=pinned` but config not enabled in phase 1. we can flip it once we agree on canonical settings.

Logan Wright: if you create a separate scheduler_mode label value, confirm it’s within cardinality budget (ok if bounded).

deploy-bot: Rollback complete in us-east.
- Service: serving-runtime
- Version: 1.18.0-rc2 (git_sha=5c0a8b1)

Sean Gallagher: p95 back to within ~2% of baseline. tokens/sec back to normal too. calling mitigation successful.

incident-bot: ✅ *Alert resolved* (signal back within threshold for 3 consecutive windows)
- Slice: model=llama-3-70b-instruct region=us-east gpu_sku=A100-80GB runtime_version=1.18.0-rc2

Tomáš Novák: documenting timeline:
- 1736821902 page fired
- 1736821668 deploy rc3 annotation
- 1736822600 rollback initiated
- 1736823185 rollback complete
- 1736823500 metrics recovered

Rafael Mendes: follow-up tickets?

Sean Gallagher: creating runtime follow-up + detector note.
- ENG-2861 "Investigate heuristic_x causing p95 regression on A100 (llama-3-70b)" (assign Runtime)
- ENG-2862 "Canary: pin scheduler settings + add explicit scheduler_mode slice for experiments" (assign Marcus/Sofia)

Mateo Alvarez: please also link this incident in the main epic ENG-2841 and add the kernel-id note.

Hiro Tanaka: i’ll attach kernel selection evidence + trace ids to ENG-2861.

Nadia Rahman: i’ll add a note in metric validation doc that this was a real regression (not aggregation), and confirm the suppression behavior worked as expected.

Allison Grant: removed maintenance window early since rollback done.

Sean Gallagher: closing SEV-3. thanks all.
